SUBJECT's personnel security file was reviewed to identify any prior investigations or clearance determinations. At that time, SUBJECT was employed by Accenture Corporation and required a Secret-level clearance to support Department of Defense contract work. The investigation resulted in a favorable determination, and SUBJECT was granted a Secret clearance effective April 15, 2018. The clearance was valid for a period of six years and was scheduled to expire on April 14, 2024.

Records indicated that SUBJECT's Secret clearance expired on April 14, 2024, approximately three months prior to the initiation of the present investigation. SUBJECT's current application seeks a Top Secret clearance in connection with a position with the United States Customs and Border Protection (CBP) agency. No adverse findings or derogatory information were noted in the file from the 2018 investigation. The investigator noted that SUBJECT's clearance history demonstrates prior eligibility for access to classified information and a track record of maintaining security protocols during the previous six-year clearance period. [April 15, 2024] [CBI02847]

The investigator noted that SUBJECT maintains stable housing and vehicle financing consistent with SUBJECT's reported income level. # Unemployment (VIII)

SUBJECT's employment history was reviewed to identify any gaps between positions and to assess the continuity of his professional career. The investigation revealed four positions spanning from September 2009 to the present, with SUBJECT currently employed as an IT Systems Administrator at ManTech International in Tucson, Arizona, since March 1, 2024.

SUBJECT's first professional position began at Portland State University IT Department as a Student Employee IT Help Desk Technician, commencing September 1, 2009, and concluding June 30, 2011, upon his graduation. Records confirmed this employment was concurrent with his undergraduate studies at Portland State University (September 2007 to May 2011). SUBJECT departed this position due to graduation and transition to full-time employment, which is consistent with typical career progression for student employees.

SUBJECT's next position was with TechCore Solutions in Portland, Oregon, as an IT Support Specialist, beginning June 1, 2014. However, a gap of approximately two years and eight months exists between SUBJECT's departure from Portland State University on June 30, 2011, and his start date at TechCore Solutions on June 1, 2014. During the subject interview conducted on February 14, 2024, SUBJECT was asked to account for this period. SUBJECT stated that he relocated to Seattle, Washington, in July 2011 to pursue additional technical certifications and training through various online platforms and community college courses. SUBJECT indicated he worked part-time in retail and customer service positions during this interval to support himself financially but did not provide employer names or contact information for these positions. SUBJECT acknowledged that he did not list these part-time positions on his employment history form, characterizing them as temporary and not relevant to his professional IT career trajectory. When pressed for specific details regarding the locations and dates of these positions, SUBJECT became less forthcoming and stated that employment records from that period were likely no longer available. This gap and SUBJECT's vague accounting for the 2011-2014 period warrant further investigation and verification through alternative records sources.

SUBJECT's employment at TechCore Solutions commenced June 1, 2014, and concluded July 14, 2018, a continuous period of approximately four years and one month. SUBJECT departed this position to accept a Senior Systems Analyst role at Accenture in Phoenix, Arizona, with an effective start date of July 15, 2018, representing a seamless transition with no gap between positions. Records confirmed the employment dates and the reason for leaving, which SUBJECT cited as career advancement with higher compensation and growth potential.

SUBJECT's tenure at Accenture spanned July 15, 2018, through March 31, 2023, a period of approximately four years and eight months. SUBJECT's employment records and separation documentation indicated that his position was eliminated due to company restructuring and cost reduction initiatives. However, during the subject interview, SUBJECT initially characterized his departure as a voluntary resignation to pursue other opportunities, stating he had grown dissatisfied with the corporate environment and sought a role with greater technical involvement. When presented with the company's separation records indicating a layoff, SUBJECT acknowledged the position elimination but maintained that he had been considering departure prior to the layoff announcement. This discrepancy between SUBJECT's initial account and the documented separation reason has been noted for adjudicator review.

A gap of approximately eleven months exists between SUBJECT's separation from Accenture on March 31, 2023, and his current position start date at ManTech International on March 1, 2024. During the subject interview, SUBJECT was questioned regarding this employment gap. SUBJECT stated that he utilized this period to relocate from Phoenix to Tucson, complete the CompTIA Security+ Certification (which records confirm he completed between March 1, 2019, and June 15, 2019, prior to the Accenture separation), and conduct an intentional job search to identify a position aligned with his career objectives. SUBJECT stated he was selective in his job applications and preferred to secure a role in the government contracting sector rather than accept interim employment. SUBJECT provided documentation of his job search activities, including email correspondence with recruiters and applications to several defense contracting firms. Investigator review of these materials confirmed that SUBJECT maintained active communication with recruiters during the 2023-2024 gap period. However, SUBJECT did not provide documentation of unemployment benefits applications or receipt during this eleven-month period, and when asked whether he had applied for such benefits, SUBJECT stated he was uncertain of his eligibility and did not pursue them. Financial records obtained through SUBJECT's authorization revealed no significant income deposits during this period, though records showed SUBJECT maintained a savings account balance of approximately $47,000 at the time of his separation from Accenture, which would have provided financial resources to sustain him during the employment gap.

SUBJECT's current position at ManTech International commenced March 1, 2024, as an IT Systems Administrator managing and maintaining Customs and Border Protection (CBP) IT infrastructure. Verification contact was attempted with SUBJECT's current supervisor, Diana Prince, IT Operations Manager at ManTech International, on February 28, 2024. Ms. Prince confirmed SUBJECT's employment dates and current position responsibilities. Ms. Prince indicated extensive contact (daily to 3x week) as supervisor from March 1, 2024, to present, and characterized SUBJECT as competent and reliable in his technical responsibilities. However, Ms. Prince noted that SUBJECT has been absent from the office on several occasions without advance notice and that SUBJECT's timekeeping has been inconsistent. Ms. Prince stated that while SUBJECT's technical performance is satisfactory, she had initiated a preliminary discussion with human resources regarding attendance and punctuality expectations. This information regarding attendance issues has been documented for adjudicator consideration.

In summary, SUBJECT's employment history reflects a generally progressive career trajectory in information technology, with advancement in position level and compensation over time. However, three matters require adjudicator attention: (1) a two-year-eight-month employment gap between 2011 and 2014 that SUBJECT did not adequately document or provide verifiable detail regarding; (2) a discrepancy between SUBJECT's initial characterization of his Accenture departure as voluntary and the documented record indicating a layoff; and (3) an eleven-month employment gap in 2023-2024 following his Accenture separation, during which SUBJECT maintained financial resources but did not pursue unemployment benefits. Additionally, recent concerns regarding attendance and punctuality at SUBJECT's current position have been noted by his supervisor. These matters are presented for adjudicator evaluation in the context of SUBJECT's overall employment reliability and truthfulness.
